injuries.name: A.J. Greer
injuries.note: Greer suffered an upper-body injury in Sunday's 6-3 win over Ottawa. He will miss at least the next four games, starting with Tuesday's matchup against Vancouver, but it's unclear when he will be ready to return. Greer has four goals, six points, 23 shots on net and 36 hits in 13 appearances this season.

injuries.name: Troy Terry
injuries.note: "Troy is closer. When I say closer, hopefully, definitely, in the next, I'm gonna say, week or so," Quenneville told Lee. Terry hasn't played yet this campaign because of the injury. He had 19 goals and 57 points in 61 regular-season outings in 2025-26. The 29-year-old is expected to take on a top-six role once he's healthy.

injuries.name: Ian Moore
injuries.note: Moore has been on injured reserve since the start of the regular season due to a lower-body injury he sustained on the first day of training camp. While he was given a return timetable of 2-4 weeks in mid-September, he's slated to miss more time than that, and he seems to have several steps to clear before he's in the mix to return to game action.

injuries.name: Ryan Poehling
injuries.note: Poehling was placed on injured reserve Tuesday morning, and the specifics of his injury have revealed that he's set to likely be sidelined into late November. In his absence, Roger McQueen, the 10th overall pick from the 2025 NHL Entry Draft, is expected to play in the team's middle six up the center of the ice. The 27-year-old Poehling was off to a solid start to the 2026-27 campaign prior to going down, posting a pair of points and solid category-coverage numbers across five games.

injuries.name: Filip Chytil
injuries.note: Given that Chytil landed on injured reserve Oct. 30, he was only eligible to appear in the Canucks' second contest of the team's upcoming two-game road trip. When healthy this season, the 27-year-old center has posted two points, 13 shots on net and six blocked shots over seven appearances. Once the Canucks' return to Vancouver, Chytil's first opportunity to be activated from injured reserve and make his return is Monday's clash against the Flyers.

injuries.name: Thatcher Demko
injuries.note: Demko missed the second half of the 2025-26 season after undergoing hip surgery in January, and he was officially placed on injured reserve last week. He doesn't yet have a clear timetable for when he'll be back in action, but Sedin said that Demko is "taking steps every day" in his recovery process. While Demko is sidelined, Kevin Lankinen and Leevi Merilainen should compete for starts in the Canucks' crease.

injuries.name: A.J. Greer
injuries.note: Upper-Body: The Anaheim Ducks placed F A.J. Greer on injured reserve on Monday (Nov. 2).

injuries.name: Ian Moore
injuries.note: Lower-body: The Ducks said on Friday (Oct. 16) that Moore remains without timetable to return.

injuries.name: Ryan Poehling
injuries.note: Lower-Body: The Ducks said on Tuesday (Oct. 13) that Poehling is expected to miss 6-8 weeks with an MCL sprain.

injuries.name: Troy Terry
injuries.note: Hip: The Anaheim Ducks said on Saturday (Oct. 31) that Terry's return doesn't appear to be imminent, he is getting close to playing, per Derek Lee of The Hockey News.

injuries.name: Filip Chytil
injuries.note: Upper Body: The Vancouver Canucks said on Tuesday (Nov. 3) that Chytil won't travel with the team during their upcoming two-game road trip, per Jeff Paterson of CanucksArmy.com.

injuries.name: Thatcher Demko
injuries.note: Hip: The Canucks placed Demko on injured reserve and hopeful he will be ready to return before Christmas, per Kevin Woodley of NHL.com.

injuries.name: Mackenzie MacEachern
injuries.note: Undisclosed: The Vancouver Canucks placed F Mackenzie MacEachern on injured reserve non-roster.

injuries.name: Akil Thomas
injuries.note: Undisclosed: The Vancouver Canucks placed F Akil Thomas on injured reserve non-roster.

injuries.name: Tom Willander
injuries.note: Lower Body: Willander tweaked something in Tuesday's (Nov. 3) morning skate and won't play versus the Ducks, Canucks play-by-play announcer Brendan Batchelor reports.
